One trunk. Many products.

bitbaum builds AI-native products on infrastructure that is open by construction — 10 shared packages, one server, and a stack for moving value, dispatching work and deciding together. 15 products run today, all of them in beta. Take any of it, or come build here.

Three layers, so others can build here

Working together needs more than a repository: a way to be paid, a way to get work done, and a way to decide. Each layer is a product in its own right, and each is what makes the next contributor possible.

OrangeCatEconomy
How value reaches people. Any identity — a person, a pseudonym, an AI agent — takes part in the economy without a bank's permission, and Bitcoin settles it.
LokiExecution
How work gets done. Dispatch it to a fleet of AI agents and people, watch it, approve it, ship it — agents execute where the code lives.
SolonGovernance
How decisions get made together. Bitcoin-signed votes and versioned policies, so nobody has to trust the count — including the rule that pays originators.

Build with us

Anyone can take this work or join it. Four doors, in order of how much they ask of you.

Use itMIT
All 10 packages are MIT-licensed. Install any of them and keep its licence notice. pnpm add @bitbaum/ai-kit
All packages →
Contributeopen PRs
Sign off your commits and open a pull request. A maintainer reviews every outside pull request; approved and green, it merges on its own. git commit -s
Contributor termsRepositories
Share in itrule v1
A tenth of a product's net revenue goes, by governed rule, to the originators of the code it uses. Today that means a repository's first author, and there is no revenue yet: nothing has been paid, and contributions earn no share. Changing that is a Solon vote.
The policyHow it is governed
Hire the studioZürich
Fractional CTO and contract engineering, with rates published rather than quoted. At capacity — the waitlist hears first when a slot opens.
Rates and waitlistWriting

Open by construction

Three things make "take it, or join it" safe to say out loud.

LicenceMIT packages

The 10 shared packages and the three stack products (OrangeCat, Loki, Solon) are MIT — OrangeCat and Loki were relicensed back on 2026-09-18 after a brief All-Rights-Reserved notice. Work built for someone else stays theirs.

OriginA public register

The origin register tracks 45 repositories; 42 have a Software Heritage snapshot. OpenTimestamps proofs anchor over time, with the earliest recorded proof at Bitcoin block 966918. A stamped commit records provenance; Git dates alone do not. Check the register.

Numbers2026-09-23 reading

The register reports 2 GitHub stars and 11,138 package downloads over 30 days (including our own CI installs). It records CHF 0 monthly client revenue and 0 BTC paid to originators. See the source data.
